question.prompt:
Agnes writes the following four statements on a blank piece of paper.

• At least one of these statements is true.

• At least two of these statements are true.

• At least two of these statements are false.

• At least one of these statements is false.

Each statement is either true or false. How many false statements did Agnes write on the paper?

solutions.title: Test the third statement
solutions.explanation:
The third statement is especially restrictive: if it were true, the fourth statement would also be true, because at least two false statements would imply at least one false statement.

But then the third and fourth statements would provide two true statements. That would make both the first and second statements true as well. All four statements would be true, contradicting the third statement's claim that at least two are false.

Therefore the third statement is false. Its claim, “at least two are false,” fails, so there is at most one false statement. Since the third statement itself is false, there is exactly one.

This is consistent: the first and second statements are true because there are three true statements, and the fourth is true because there is one false statement. The answer is \(\boxed{1}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
